decisions.reason: As a very recent extension of the established spraying portfolio, management would keep it because development and launch resources have just been committed and any weak early traction can still be seen as a temporary market ramp-up issue.

Management would keep this low-pressure injection pump because it is close to the core business, was visibly committed to with its own webpage, and abandoning it after only one year would undermine justification of the launch investment.

Management would keep this transfer pump since it builds directly on the firm’s established offer and the short time on the market makes it easy to attribute any initial shortcomings to normal commercialization delays rather than product failure.

Management would keep fire protection flow monitoring because it received a visible standalone presentation and aligns strongly with the firm’s announced move toward future-oriented, more digitalized and interoperable customer solutions.
